nodes.summary: Over the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the single-bit words form the language $\{0, 1\}$ whose only words are the one-letter words $0$ and $1$.
nodes.title: Single-bit words

nodes.summary: Over the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the bit words form the language $\{0, 1\}^*$ of all finite words, including the empty word, all of whose letters are bits.
nodes.title: Bit words

nodes.summary: Each boolean $b$ (with false read as $0$ and true as $1$) is sent to the corresponding bit letter of the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$.
nodes.title: Bits as letters

nodes.summary: Over the alphabet consisting of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, let $u, u'$ be words over $T$ and $v, v'$ words over the bits. If $u \# v = u' \# v'$, then $u = u'$ and $v = v'$.
nodes.title: Unique decomposition at the separator

nodes.summary: There is a finite alphabet $T$, with a primitive recursive encoding and decidable equality, such that no multi-stack Turing machine decides, for an encoded context-free grammar $g$ over $T$, whether the language of $g$ is regular.
nodes.title: Regularity of context-free languages is undecidable

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet and $L$ a language over $T$. Over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the language $L \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, of the words $u \# v$ with $u$ a word over $T$, $v$ a word over the bits, and $u \in L$ or $v = 0^n 1^n$ for some $n$, is regular if and only if $L$ contains every word over $T$.
nodes.title: Regularity of the reduction language characterises universality

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet and $L$ a language over $T$ that contains every word over $T$. Over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the language $L \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, which here equals $T^* \# \{0,1\}^*$, is regular.
nodes.title: The reduction language of a universal language is regular

Assign to the nonterminals of $G$ the languages $V(0) = L(g) \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, where $L(g)$ is the language of $g$,…
nodes.title: Every production of the regularity grammar is sound for its intended languages

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$ with decidable equality, with language $L(g)$. Over the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, the regularity grammar of $g$ generates exactly $L(g) \# \{0,1\}^* \cup T^* \# \{0^n 1^n : n \ge 0\}$, the set of words $u \# v$ with $u$ a word over $T$, $v$ a word over the bits, and $u \in L(g)$ or $v = 0^n 1^n$ for some $n$.
nodes.title: The language of the regularity grammar

nodes.summary: This is the language over the alphabet $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ of the reduction from universality to regularity consisting of the one-letter words $t$ with $t \in T$.
nodes.title: One-letter words over $T$

nodes.summary: This is the language $T^*$ over the alphabet $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ of the reduction from universality to regularity: the words, including the empty word, all of whose letters lie in $T$.
nodes.title: Words over $T$ in the reduction alphabet

nodes.summary: For a type $T$, the alphabet $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ consists of the letters of $T$, a separator $\#$ and two bits $0$ and $1$, all distinct.
nodes.title: Alphabet of the reduction from universality to regularity

nodes.summary: Let $T$ be a finite alphabet with decidable equality and a primitive recursive coding, and let $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ extend $T$ by a separator $\#$ and two bits. There is a computable map $f$ from encoded context-free grammars over $T$ to encoded context-free grammars over $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ such that a grammar $g$ generates every word over $T$ if and only if the language generated by $f(g)$ is regular.
nodes.title: Universality many-one reduces to regularity of context-free languages

nodes.summary: Let $L$ be a language over an alphabet $T$, let $T \sqcup \{\#, 0, 1\}$ extend $T$ by a separator $\#$ and two bits, and let $R(L) = L\,\#\,\{0,1\}^* \cup T^*\,\#\,\{0^n1^n : n \in \mathbb{N}\}$ over this alphabet. If some word $u$ over $T$ is not in $L$, then $R(L)$ is not regular.

nodes.title: Languages assigned to the nonterminals of the regularity grammar

nodes.summary: For an alphabet $T$, among the letters of the reduction (the letters of $T$, a separator and two bits), this is the separator, written $\#$.
nodes.title: The separator letter

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$, and let $n$ be a nonterminal of $g$. If $g$ derives a word $u$ over $T$ from $n$, then the regularity grammar of $g$ derives from its nonterminal $n + 4$ the word $u$ read over the extended alphabet, each letter $t$ of $T$ replaced by the corresponding letter.

nodes.title: Shifting a symbol into the regularity grammar

nodes.title: Alphabet letters in the extended alphabet

nodes.summary: Let $g$ be an encoded context-free grammar over a finite alphabet $T$. Then $g$ generates every word over $T$ if and only if the regularity grammar of $g$ generates a regular language.
nodes.title: A grammar is universal iff its regularity grammar generates a regular language

Theory of Computation

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
